requirement: The database must securely associate every search activity, result, provider configuration, and authentication token with a specific user owner to enforce ownership and access control. For OAuth tokens, each user may have at most one token per identity provider to prevent duplicate credentials. Query-related text fields across searches and results must have a defined maximum length to maintain consistency across provider connectors. The system must also track the lifecycle of searches (including status transitions), record which providers were used, and retain provider-specific configuration details such as connector type, authentication method, and processing pipelines.
workload: Retrieve all active SearchProviders that are either owned by the given user or marked as shared, to determine which providers a user can federate a search to.
Count the number of searches created per day over the last 30 days, ordered chronologically, for admin analytics dashboard.
Retrieve the cached RAG result (generated by ChatGPT) for a given search, to serve the AI summary without regenerating.

Identify futile searches: searches that completed with status FULL_RESULTS_READY or PARTIAL_RESULTS_READY in a given time window but have no associated Result rows with retrieved > 0, returning search id, query, owner_id, and creation date.
